html:
The Siletz were the southernmost division of the Tillamook people of the northern Oregon coast, speaking their own dialect of the Salishan Tillamook language and living on the Siletz River. The name later passed to the Siletz Reservation, set up in 1855 on this coast as part of the Coast Reservation.

After the Rogue River Wars, members of more than twenty peoples of western Oregon and northern California were moved there, among them the Tututni, Takelma and Coquille. The reservation was cut down by land sales and opened to settlers. The US ended recognition of the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians in 1954 and restored it in 1977. To the north lived the Nehalem.
